answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks using trust-graph routing, bounding network influence along verified peer edges. As random walks wander across the graph, synthetic clusters cannot amplify authority because adversaries incur the scarce cost of securing authentic trust edges from honest peers. Without valid links, malicious weight drops to a nadir before fraudulent activity can spiral across the ecosystem. However, this approach penalizes honest newcomers facing cold-start barriers.
